sections.title: Cultural concepts
sections.content:
Vocabulary for discussing culture and diversity:
• multicultural — including people of many different cultures. London is one of the most multicultural cities in the world.
• stereotype — an oversimplified idea about a group. We should challenge stereotypes rather than accept them.
• assimilate — absorb into a wider culture. Immigrants often face pressure to assimilate quickly.
• inclusive — not excluding any group. The company promotes an inclusive workplace culture.
• discrimination — unfair treatment based on group identity. Discrimination based on gender or race is illegal.

sections.title: Intercultural skills
sections.content:
Skills for interacting across cultures:
• empathy — understanding others' feelings. Empathy is essential for building cross-cultural relationships.
• tolerance — accepting differences. Tolerance of different viewpoints enriches society.
• etiquette — conventional rules of polite behaviour. Business etiquette varies significantly between countries.
• taboo — something prohibited by social custom. In some cultures, discussing money is a taboo subject.
• integration — combining different groups into one. Successful integration requires effort from both sides.

exercises.question: An oversimplified generalisation about a group is a:
exercises.explanation: A stereotype is a widely held but oversimplified image or idea about a particular group.

exercises.question: A workplace that welcomes everyone regardless of background is:
exercises.explanation: Inclusive means not excluding any section of society.

exercises.question: Something forbidden by social custom is:
exercises.explanation: A taboo is a social or religious custom prohibiting discussion of something.

exercises.question: Understanding and sharing others' feelings is:
exercises.explanation: Empathy is the ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

exercises.question: Rules of polite behaviour in social situations are:
exercises.explanation: Etiquette is the customary code of polite behaviour in society.

exercises.question: Unfair treatment of people based on their identity is:
exercises.explanation: Discrimination is the unjust treatment of different categories of people.

exercises.question: The process of adopting the culture of a wider society is:
exercises.hint: Becoming part of the dominant culture.
exercises.explanation: Assimilation is the process of absorbing into the cultural tradition of a population.

exercises.question: Accepting that others may have different beliefs is:
exercises.explanation: Tolerance is willingness to accept behaviour and beliefs different from one's own.
